- $g(4) = 1$

- $g(8) = ?$

Hmm, if $g(7)=3$ and $g(6)=3$, maybe $g(n) = \lceil n/2 \rceil - 1$? For $n=4$: $2-1=1$ ✓. $n=5$: $3-1=2$ ✓. $n=6$: $3-1=2$ ✗ (we need 3).

Or $g(n) = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$: $n=4$: 2 ✗.

Final answer: \boxed{f(n) = n - 2,\quad g(n) = \left\lceil\dfrac{n}{2}\right\rceil}
